messages.author: 11a40d58d6ce1105
messages.subject: About linear constrained GMRF sampling
parts:
Hi,

I recently looked at the INLA paper Rue et al. (2009) and found that linear constrained GMRF (Ax=e, where A is a k by n matrix of rank k) is sampled as
x^c = x - Q^{-1}A'(AQ^{-1}A')^{-1}(Ax-e)

with additional cost of O(nk^2).

I had a try with n and k are both of order 10^3, it turned out to be really time consuming..(overnight running.. not ended yet)
 
I wonder if A here is a sparse matrix ( however in inla.spde2.matern, extraconstr has to be class "matrix" so that a sparse matrix of class "dgCMatrix" can not be asigned.. right? ), would it be quicker?
 
Many thanks!
Xiao GUO

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] About linear constrained GMRF sampling
parts:
In INLA, it is implicitly assumed that the number of constraints is small.  When that is no longer true, it is still possible to solve the problem using the techniques here http://dev.journal.austms.org.au/ojs/index.php/ANZIAMJ/article/view/131

(Essentially the same idea expressed in a different way is http://www.math.umt.edu/bardsley/papers/RTO.pdf)

All of these methods will work as long as the constraint matrix A is sparse.  If it isn't than nothing will work.  

Best wishes,

Dan

> x^c = x - Q^{-1}A'(AQ^{-1}A')^{-1}(Ax-e)
>
>
> with additional cost of O(nk^2).
>
>
> I had a try with n and k are both of order 10^3, it turned out to be

is efficient if k is small and less efficient if k is O(n), which is
your case.

there is a 'bad sign' if your model require 10^3's linear constraints,
is there some way you could reformulate it so you do not need all of
them?

Best
H

messages.author: 11a40d58d6ce1105
messages.subject: Re: About linear constrained GMRF sampling
parts:
Thank you all!
I am afraid that it is difficult to reduce the number of constraints in some cases..

Just one suggestion (not necessarily): Daniel gave some literatures/techniques on efficient sampling with NOT small number of constraints, INLA might take advantage of these techniques so that it is able to handle problems with large number of linear constraints.
 
Many thanks!
Xiao GUO
